title: The Doubling Lantern Moths
story: The Moonwell Gardens are famous for their silver pears — until Pirrowlace arrives, a brood of 7 glowing lantern moths that eats blossoms and doubles its number every 12 minutes. Swatting them only makes them split faster, so Mr 6 sheathes his sword and gets out his netting thread, because he must weave one net big enough for the whole swarm one full hour from now.
question: How many lantern moths will there be after 60 minutes?
solution: After one hour the brood will number 224 moths.
praise: Doubling again and again was absolutely the right idea — the only slip was counting how many doublings fit in the hour (60 / 12 = 5, not 4 or 6).
hint: How many 12-minute chunks fit inside 60 minutes? Double the starting 7 that many times.
victory: Mr 6 wove a net for exactly 224 moths, and when the glowing brood filled it to the last wing, he hung the whole shimmering bundle in the orchard as a lantern. Pirrowlace is now the best night-light the gardeners have ever had.
imagePrompt: A moonlit pear orchard swarming with hundreds of softly glowing lantern moths while a small caped numeral-six knight calmly weaves an enormous silver net between two trees.
